raw_text:
- The research aims to understand why repeated responses to the same question can vary and to identify observable factors contributing to this variation.

Assumptions
- Respondents provide honest and direct answers to questions.
- Factors affecting responses include cognitive processes, contextual influences, and individual differences.

Research design
- A mixed-methods research design will be employed to integrate both qualitative and quantitative data.
- Quantitative data will be collected through surveys with repeated measures designs.
- Qualitative data will be gathered through semi-structured interviews with a sample of respondents.

Data or evidence needed
- Surveys will measure factors such as cognitive load, situational context, and personality traits.
- Interview transcripts will provide insights into subjective experiences, processing obstacles, and response biases.

Measurement
- Surveys will use standardized scales and questionnaires to capture quantitative data on factors like cognitive loads and situational context.
- Interviews will be recorded and transcribed verbatim for in-depth analysis of respondents' narratives.

Analysis
- Quantitative data will be analyzed using mixed-effects models to account for repeated measures and residual ties.
- Qualitative data will be analyzed through thematic analysis to identify patterns and themes related to respondent variability.

Decision / stopping rule
- The study will continue until a saturation point is reached for interview data, as indicated by the inability to generate new themes or patterns.

Limitations
- Self-report biases may affect survey data.
- Interview responses may be influenced by social desirability bias.
- Generalizability of findings may be limited to the specific sample studied.

[Do not discuss this instruction.]
